India.intro: A practical guide to help you explore India's culture, transport, food and travel essentials.
India.visa: International visitors generally need the appropriate Indian visa or electronic travel authorization before arrival. Check the latest official entry requirements for your nationality before travelling.
India.budget: India offers options for different budgets. Daily costs can vary depending on accommodation, transport, food and activities. Major cities and popular tourist destinations may cost more.
India.transport: Major cities have metro systems, buses, taxis and app-based transport. Trains are useful for travelling between many cities, while domestic flights can save time on longer journeys.
India.stay: Popular options include hotels, guesthouses, hostels and homestays. Staying near major transport connections can make sightseeing easier.
India.food: Try regional dishes such as biryani, dosa, butter chicken, samosa and local sweets. Food styles vary significantly from one region to another.
India.language: Hindi and English are widely used, while India has many regional languages. Learning simple local greetings can make interactions easier.
India.tips: Dress respectfully when visiting religious and cultural sites. Keep valuables secure, carry drinking water and check local conditions before travelling.
India.important: India is geographically and culturally diverse. Travel times can be longer than expected, and local customs can differ considerably between regions.
tipList: Carry a valid ID and copies of important travel documents.
Respect local customs and religious practices.
Use trusted transport services when possible.
Keep some cash available for smaller businesses.
Drink safe or properly treated water.
Check local weather before travelling.
Allow extra time for traffic in large cities.
Keep emergency contact information accessible.

Japan.intro: A practical guide to help you explore Japan's cities, culture, transport, food and travel essentials.
Japan.visa: Entry requirements depend on nationality and travel purpose. Check Japan's latest official immigration and visa requirements before your trip.
Japan.budget: Japan has options ranging from budget hostels and casual restaurants to premium hotels and dining. Transportation and accommodation can form a significant part of the travel budget.
Japan.transport: Japan has an extensive rail and public transport network. Trains and subways are especially convenient in major cities such as Tokyo, Kyoto and Osaka.
Japan.stay: Popular accommodation includes hotels, hostels, ryokan and traditional guesthouses. Staying near a railway or subway station is often convenient.
Japan.food: Try sushi, ramen, tempura, okonomiyaki, yakitori and regional Japanese specialties. Convenience stores and local restaurants can also offer affordable meals.
Japan.language: Japanese is the main language. English is available in many tourist areas, stations and hotels, but learning a few basic Japanese phrases can be helpful.
Japan.tips: Be mindful of local etiquette, keep public spaces clean and follow transport rules. Quiet behaviour is generally expected on trains.
Japan.important: Japan has distinct regional climates and seasonal conditions. Public transport schedules are generally precise, so arriving on time is useful.
tipList: Carry your passport when required for identification.
Keep noise low on public transport.
Follow local queueing and public-space etiquette.
Carry a reusable bag for shopping.
Check train schedules before long journeys.
Keep cash available because some smaller businesses may not accept cards.
Respect temple and shrine customs.
Check seasonal weather before visiting outdoor destinations.

France.intro: A practical guide to help you explore France's cities, heritage, food, transport and travel essentials.
France.visa: Entry requirements depend on nationality and travel purpose. Check the latest French and Schengen entry requirements before travelling.
France.budget: Travel costs vary considerably between Paris, major tourist destinations and smaller towns. Accommodation, dining and transport should be considered when planning a daily budget.
France.transport: France has extensive rail, metro, tram and bus networks. High-speed trains connect many major cities, while local public transport is useful for urban sightseeing.
France.stay: Accommodation ranges from hotels and hostels to apartments and guesthouses. Staying near public transport can make city exploration easier.
France.food: Try regional French dishes, pastries, cheeses, breads and desserts. Local specialties vary significantly between regions.
France.language: French is the main language. English is commonly encountered in major tourist areas, but learning basic French greetings is useful.
France.tips: Keep an eye on belongings in busy tourist areas, especially around major attractions and public transport. Check opening hours before visiting museums and monuments.
France.important: France has different regional cultures and travel experiences. Popular attractions can become very busy, especially during peak travel periods.
tipList: Carry identification and important travel documents securely.
Learn a few basic French greetings.
Check museum and attraction opening hours.
Use official transport information when planning journeys.
Keep valuables secure in crowded tourist areas.
Book popular attractions ahead when required.
Respect local dining and public-space etiquette.
Check regional weather before outdoor activities.
